_comment: Wiring and consumption audits that decide from raw python source text, as they stand on the tree invocation_proved_by_parse_not_by_text.py shipped with. MAY ONLY SHRINK; a row matching nothing is rc 1. Each closes by parsing the caller and deciding from the syntax tree, and by reporting a prose-only occurrence as its own outcome. Hand-authored from --json; there is no --write-baseline.

known.reason: THE INSTANCE THE CAPTURE MEASURED. Its own docstring says a step with no dispatching producer 'can only ever be MISSING, and that is the root cause of middle steps silently skipped' — and it concatenates seven runner sources and applies regular expressions to the result, with no syntax-tree parse anywhere in the module. Measured corpus: 3,055,921 bytes of which 1,472,929 (48%) are docstring and comment, so a name in prose is graded as a call. On the same commit three producers declared by two path steps appear ZERO times in any runner, in code or in prose.

Reads a schema module's source and extracts a mapping by regular expression. A mapping shown in an example inside a docstring is indistinguishable from the real one.
Reads gate program sources and decides contract compliance by regular expression over the raw text, so a contract line quoted in a docstring counts as the contract being met.
